sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A creeping or ascending perennial herb native to Africa and nearby islands, now found in several tropical regions. It reaches about 0.5 m tall and may spread 1 m wide.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: The compound leaves usually have five to seven leaflets. Small pink flowers grow in clusters and are followed by narrow pods.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: Severe poisonings have been reported in horses and other livestock. Sources sometimes note confusion with I. hendecaphylla; do not use this plant as fodder or consume it.
